assertion_analysis.failure_condition: fails if a later figure review supersedes an earlier text review of the same run: with the rubric dropped from _run_subject the text record reads SUPERSEDED instead of ANSWERED. Demonstrated red by negative-control-no-rubric.log.

fails if _run_subject stops keying the family on the rubric, if the figure rubric constant changes name, or if a non-figure rubric is grouped with the figure family; the 'figure' literal at :182 is independent of review_module.FIGURE_REVIEW_RUBRIC, so it pins the contract rather than echoing it.

fails if dispatch order stops deciding within one rubric, or if the family comparison starts grouping different rubrics together; both records are stored through the store's writer with explicit dispatched_at, so the ordering is a fixture fact, not wall clock.

a text-only run must be unchanged: without a figure record, the later text review supersedes the earlier, and the blocking finding reads OPEN; it fails if the new subject grouping also splits text reviews.

findings.text: _is_figure_review normalises the rubric field itself (str(record.get('rubric') or '').strip().lower()) rather than calling the owner of that read, reckon/crew/review.py:2193 _review_record_rubric (whose sibling _review_rubric_matches at :2200 computes the same figure-or-not predicate); the constant is shared so the value cannot drift, but the normalisation now exists in two places.
